summary: DeterminismContract.validateStringArray() does not enforce the project's plain/no-execute data boundary before evaluating array structure. It accepts any table and immediately executes `#parts`; current Luau implements table `__len`, so a metatable-backed parts/scopes table can run caller code before canonical StableId/seed validation rejects or accepts it. Subsequent indexed reads can likewise reach metatable behavior if raw fields are absent. This affects exported encodeParts/hashParts/stableId/seedFor call paths and should be fixed/tested independently of PR #306's schema-key formatting repair.
evidence: main@aa7e04f05834ae783773c908fccfdbbe510558e5 src/shared/Core/DeterminismContract.luau validateStringArray() checks only type(parts) == 'table' before `local length = #parts`; there is no getmetatable(parts) == nil preflight.
The same helper is exported transitively through encodeParts(), hashParts(), stableId(), and seedFor(); StableId.fromParts() forwards caller arrays directly to DeterminismContract.stableId().
Current tests/deterministic_rng.luau and tests/stable_id_headless.luau contain no metatable/no-execute regression for these array inputs.
Luau's implemented table-length contract calls a table's __len metamethod for the # operator, so this is an executable rejection boundary rather than only a shape-policy inconsistency.

metadata.recommendedRegression: metatable-backed parts/scopes with hostile __len must reject with zero metamethod executions; inert/protected metatables must also reject to lock the plain-data contract
